title: Prime localization and residue fibres of a scalar-extended module
statement:
Let $f:A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, $M$ an $A$-module and $N=M\otimes_AB$, with $B$ acting on the second factor [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Let $\mathfrak q\subset B$ be prime and $\mathfrak p=f^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$. Use prime localizations $A_{\mathfrak p},B_{\mathfrak q}$ and residue fields $\kappa(\mathfrak p)=\operatorname{Frac}(A/\mathfrak p)$, $\kappa(\mathfrak q)=\operatorname{Frac}(B/\mathfrak q)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and module localizations [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. The induced map $f_{\mathfrak q}:A_{\mathfrak p}\to B_{\mathfrak q}$ is local (the inverse image of the maximal ideal is the maximal ideal) and induces a field homomorphism $\bar f:\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$. There are canonical isomorphisms
$$\Phi:N_{\mathfrak q}\xrightarrow{\sim}M_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_{A_{\mathfrak p}}B_{\mathfrak q},\qquad (m\otimes b)/t\longmapsto(m/1)\otimes(b/t),$$
$$\Psi:(M_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_{A_{\mathfrak p}}\kappa(\mathfrak p))\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}\kappa(\mathfrak q)\xrightarrow{\sim}N_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{B_{\mathfrak q}}\kappa(\mathfrak q).$$
Here $\Phi$ is $B_{\mathfrak q}$-linear, $\Psi$ is $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$-linear, and
$$\Psi(((m/s)\otimes u)\otimes v)=((m\otimes1)/1)\otimes\bigl(\bar f(u)v/\overline{f(s)}\bigr)\quad(s\notin\mathfrak p).$$
The map $\Psi$ agrees with the map obtained by tensoring $\Phi^{-1}$ with $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ and using tensor associativity. No flatness or finite generation hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Put $S=A\setminus\mathfrak p$, $T=B\setminus\mathfrak q$, $A'=A_{\mathfrak p}$ and $B'=B_{\mathfrak q}$. Since $f(S)\subseteq T$, the ring localization universal property gives $f_{\mathfrak q}(a/s)=f(a)/f(s)$. A fraction $a/s$ belongs to $\mathfrak pA'$ exactly when $a\in\mathfrak p$: one implication is immediate, and clearing an equality with a fraction whose numerator is in $\mathfrak p$ gives $ua\in\mathfrak p$ for $u\notin\mathfrak p$, hence $a\in\mathfrak p$. The same argument applies in $B'$. Thus $f_{\mathfrak q}^{-1}(\mathfrak qB')=\mathfrak pA'$. Quotienting gives $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to l=\kappa(\mathfrak q)$, denoted $\bar f$. Explicitly the residue of $a/s$ goes to the residue of $f(a)/f(s)$. The identification $A'/\mathfrak pA'=\operatorname{Frac}(A/\mathfrak p)$ sends the residue of $a/s$ to $\bar a/\bar s$: both sides have these fractions, and equality on either side is the condition $as'-a's\in\mathfrak p$. The analogous identification holds for $B'$. These formulas therefore give the stated field map.

Apply localization-tensor compatibility with base ring $C$, algebra $C$, multiplicative subset $C\setminus\mathfrak r$, first module $C$ and second module $P$. It gives $(C\otimes_CP)_{\mathfrak r}\cong C_{\mathfrak r}\otimes_CP$. The tensor unit $C\otimes_CP\cong P$, $c\otimes x\mapsto cx$, and tensor symmetry give $e_{P,\mathfrak r}:P_{\mathfrak r}\cong P\otimes_CC_{\mathfrak r}$, with $x/s\mapsto x\otimes(1/s)$. The units and symmetry used here have inverse formulas $x\mapsto1\otimes x$ and $x\otimes y\mapsto y\otimes x$; they respect the tensor relations and are inverse on the generating pure tensors. Localizing the unit and its inverse gives inverse maps by the fraction formula for localization. Use this construction for $(C,P,\mathfrak r)=(A,M,\mathfrak p)$ and $(B,N,\mathfrak q)$. The displayed map is $C_{\mathfrak r}$-linear: multiplying $x/s$ by $a/t$ sends both sides to $ax\otimes1/(ts)$.

source.place: Tag 00DK (lemma-tensor-localization), formula and proof; symmetry and units from Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product)

proof.text: Write $L=M\otimes_AB'$. Base change in stages gives $c_B:N\otimes_BB'\cong L$ and $c_A:(M\otimes_AA')\otimes_{A'}B'\cong L$, both sending $(m\otimes a)\otimes b$ to $m\otimes ab$ through the appropriate structure map. The two towers $A\to B\to B'$ and $A\to A'\to B'$ give the same ring map $A\to B'$, since $f_{\mathfrak q}(a/1)=f(a)/1$ by the formula of step 1, so both targets are the same $B'$-module $L$. Let $h=c_B e_{N,\mathfrak q}$ and $j=c_A(e_{M,\mathfrak p}\otimes1_{B'})$. The latter tensor map is invertible, since tensoring its explicit inverse gives an inverse on pure tensors. Thus $\Phi=j^{-1}h$ is a $B'$-linear isomorphism. On generators $h((m\otimes b)/t)=m\otimes(b/t)$ and $j((m/1)\otimes(b/t))=m\otimes(b/t)$, proving the displayed formula for $\Phi$.

source.place: Tags 00D2 (lemma-tensor-with-bimodule) and 00DK (lemma-tensor-localization), applied to the comparison in Tag 00SI

proof.text: Base change in stages for $A'\to k\to l$ gives $\alpha:(M_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_{A'}k)\otimes_kl\cong M_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_{A'}l$, with $\alpha((x\otimes u)\otimes v)=x\otimes\bar f(u)v$. The two towers $A'\to k\to l$ and $A'\to B'\to l$ give the same ring map $A'\to l$: by step 1 both send $a/s$ to the residue of $f(a)/f(s)$, so $M_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_{A'}l$ is the same module in both. For $A'\to B'\to l$ it gives $\beta:(M_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_{A'}B')\otimes_{B'}l\cong M_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_{A'}l$. Define $\Psi=(\Phi^{-1}\otimes1_l)\beta^{-1}\alpha$. All three maps are $l$-linear isomorphisms, so this gives the required isomorphism and, by its definition, precisely the asserted compatibility with tensoring $\Phi^{-1}$ and tensor associativity.

source.place: Tags 00D2 (lemma-tensor-with-bimodule) and 00SI (lemma-lci-field-change-local), displayed chain of fibre tensors

proof.text: Let $w=\bar f(u)v$ and $s\notin\mathfrak p$. In $M_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_{A'}l$, balancing gives $(m/s)\otimes w=(m/1)\otimes(w/\overline{f(s)})$, since $s/1$ maps to the nonzero element $\overline{f(s)}$ of $l$. The inverse of $\beta$ sends the latter to $((m/1)\otimes1_{B'})\otimes(w/\overline{f(s)})$. The formula for $\Phi$ in step 3 says that $\Phi^{-1}((m/1)\otimes1)=((m\otimes1)/1)$. Substitution proves the stated formula for $\Psi$ on every displayed pure tensor. No step used flatness, finite generation, or injectivity of $f$.
